title: How to access MSK services | NHS inform
text:
How to access MSK services
Musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions affect the joints, bones and muscles, and also include rarer autoimmune diseases and back pain. Common treatments for MSK conditions include:
physiotherapy
occupational therapy
hand therapy
podiatry
orthotics
Physiotherapists can help to restore movement and function when someone is affected by injury, illness or disability. They can also help to reduce your risk of injury or illness in the future.
Occupational therapy
aims to improve your ability to do everyday tasks. Occupational therapists can look at all aspects of daily life in your home, school or workplace. They look at activities you find difficult and see if there’s another way they can be done.
Hand Therapists provide assessment and treatment of many MSK hand conditions, including after injury or surgery.
They can provide advice regarding exercise, preventative care, and aids to help daily living. Depending on the condition and where you are, you may be treated by a physiotherapist or occupational therapist.
Podiatry treats abnormal conditions of the feet and lower limbs. They also prevent and correct deformity, keep you mobile and active, relieve pain and treat infections.
Orthotics use foot or heel inserts to treat problems relating to pain and discomfort in the feet, legs or spine.
Self-management
We’ve included a range of
self-management information, tools and exercises
on NHS inform to help you treat and recover from muscle, bone and joint problems and know when to seek help.
Accessing services
How you get access to MSK services depends on where you are. Your local health board decide how each service is accessed and whether you can self-refer or you would require to get a referral from a GP or other healthcare professional first.
NHS Ayrshire & Arran
Adult physiotherapy, podiatry, occupational therapy for MSK conditions, and orthotics services can only be accessed with a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
You can self-refer to paediatric physiotherapy, for a child of primary school age or below, using the self-referral form on
the NHS Ayrshire & Arran website
.
NHS Ayrshire & Arran also have the online
Musculoskeletal Service (MSK)
for information about conditions.
NHS Borders
Physiotherapy and Podiatry services can be accessed by downloading and filling in the self-referral form on the NHS Borders website. This can then be emailed or posted in using the details provided.
Physiotherapy
Children and young people’s physiotherapy
Podiatry
Podiatry for children and young people under 16
Occupational Therapy and Orthotics services can only be accessed with a referral from a healthcare professional.
NHS Dumfries & Galloway
Physiotherapy, podiatry and occupational therapy for MSK conditions can be accessed by self-referral by phoning the Dumfries and Galloway
Single Access Point on 030 33 33 3001
.
NHS Fife
Adult physiotherapy, hand therapy, occupational therapy for MSK conditions, and orthotics services can only be accessed with a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
Hand conditions
NHS Fife have a website with
information for patients who’ve been diagnosed with a hand condition
.
Podiatry
Podiatry services can be accessed by self-referral using the Request assistance form also on
the NHS Fife website
.
Children and young people
Children’s physiotherapy services can be accessed by self-referral using the request for assistance form under Referrals on
the NHS Fife website
.
A parent advice line is also available on 01592 226699. Its open:
Tuesdays from 10am to 12pm
Wednesdays from 2pm to 4pm
This is for parents who have questions about their child’s movement, mobility, development or any injuries/pain. It can also be used to access children’s occupational therapy.
NHS Forth Valley
Physiotherapy and podiatry services can only be accessed by a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
Orthotics can be accessed by self-referral using the adult or child Request for Assistance forms on
the NHS Forth Valley website
.
NHS Grampian
Physiotherapy services can be accessed by self-referral using the Self referral form on
the MSK Physio Grampian website
.
Podiatry service access depends on where in Grampian you are, details can be found on
the NHS Grampian website
.
Orthotics services can only be accessed with a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
NHS Grampian also have an
online MSK Physio service
.
NHS Greater Glasgow & Clyde
Physiotherapy services can be accessed by self-referral using the form on
the NHS Greater Glasgow & Clyde website
.
Podiatry services
can be accessed by phoning the Podiatry Appointment Hotline on 0141 347 8909.
Orthotics services
can be accessed by phoning the Referral Management Appointment Booking Centre on 0800 592087.
Orthotics services for children and young people in Greater Glasgow can be accessed by phoning the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow on 0141 452 4651. People in the Clyde area should also use the Referral Management Booking Centre.
NHS Highland
Physiotherapy, hand therapy and orthotics services can only be accessed by a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
Accessing Podiatry services can depend on where you are, details can be found on
the NHS Highland website
.
NHS Lanarkshire
Physiotherapy services can be accessed by self-referral using the online form on
the NHS Lanarkshire website
.
Physiotherapy for children and young people up to 14 can be accessed using the self-referral form on
the NHS Lanarkshire website
.
Podiatry services can be accessed by self-referral by contacting the podiatry hub on 01698 753 753 (open Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm). You can find more information on the
NHS Lanarkshire podiatry website
.
Referrals to
primary care occupational therapy
or
hand therapy
for MSK conditions can be accessed by a referral from a GP or healthcare professional, or by filling in a self-referral form at your GP practice.
NHS Lothian
Physiotherapy services can be accessed in different ways throughout the area. Not all areas accept self-referrals.
City of Edinburgh
Royal Infirmary
Western General
East Lothian
Midlothian
West Lothian
Physiotherapy services for children and young people under 18 can be accessed by self-referral by contacting the Royal Hospital for Children and Young People, Edinburgh on 0131 312 1079 or St Johns Hospital, West Lothian on 01506 522 068.
Occupational therapy, podiatry and hand therapy can only be accessed with a referral from a Healthcare Professional.
Occupational Therapy for children and young people under 18 can be accessed by contacting:
Edinburgh 0131 312 1079
East Lothian and Midlothian 0131 446 4013
West Lothian 01506 524 134
NHS Orkney
Details of how to access physiotherapy and occupational therapy are available on
the Outpatients page on the NHS Orkney website
.
To access Podiatry services you can use the self-referral form on
the NHS Orkney website
.
NHS Shetland
Physiotherapy can be accessed with a referral from a GP or health care professional, or by self-referral. The self-referral forms for both adults and children and young people can be found on the
NHS Shetland website
.
Children’s physiotherapy services can be accessed by self-referral using the form on
the NHS Shetland website
.
Podiatry can be accessed with a referral from a GP or health care professional, or by self-referral. The self-referral form can be found on
the NHS Shetland website
.
Orthotics can be accessed with a referral from a healthcare professional. If you’ve already been seen by orthotics, you can contact them on 01595 743026.
NHS Tayside
For musculoskeletal problems, such as a sore back or sports injury, you should contact your GP to make an appointment with a
First Contact Physiotherapist
.
People in Dundee, as part of a pilot project, can currently self-refer for MSK Physiotherapy using the form on the
NHS Tayside website
.
Find out which areas are covered by the Dundee HSCP
Occupational therapy and orthotics
Occupational therapy
for MSK conditions, and
orthotics services
can only be accessed by a referral from a GP or healthcare professional.
Podiatry
Information on how to access podiatry services where you are is available on
the NHS Tayside website
.
Children and young people
Find out how and where to access services for children and young people under 18 on the NHS Tayside website:
Physiotherapy
Occupational therapy
NHS Western Isles
Physiotherapy services can be accessed by self referral using the form on
the NHS Western Isles website
.
Podiatry services can be accessed by self referral using the form on
the NHS Western Isles website
.
Occupational therapy for MSK services can be accessed by self referral using the form on
the NHS Western Isles website
.
Source:
NHS 24 MSK Clinical Advisory Group
